content: Valacyclovir is a medication prescribed to treat herpes zoster (commonly known as shingles) and genital herpes. While it does not cure herpes infections, it helps reduce pain and itching, promotes the healing of sores, and prevents the formation of new sores. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Valacyclovir is available in tablet form and is taken orally. For the treatment of shingles, it is typically taken every 8 hours (three times a day) for 7 days. For the treatment of genital herpes, it is usually taken twice a day for 5 days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take valacyclovir exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. It is important to start this medication as soon as possible after symptoms appear. Continue taking valacyclovir even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking valacyclovir, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to acyclovir (Zovirax), valacyclovir, or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially cimetidine (Tagamet), probenecid (Benemid), and any vitamins. Let your doctor know if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease, immune system problems, HIV infection, or AIDS. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking valacyclovir, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Valacyclovir may cause side effects. Mild side effects include headache, upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea or loose stools, and constipation. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects require immediate medical attention and include rash, itching, confusion, yellowing of the skin or eyes, fever, and blood in the urine. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests may be ordered to monitor your response to valacyclovir. Avoid sexual intercourse when visible genital herpes lesions are present, as the infection can still be transmitted even when there are no symptoms. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of valacyclovir, contact your doctor.
